summary: A 30-foot pole L-4 lookout on the Montana-Idaho line, built in 1931 and gone by 1950; sources disagree on how it ended.

facts.design: 30-foot pole L-4 tower with a porch all the way around it
facts.status_note: Gone by 1950. Idaho Fire Lookouts says destroyed, firelookout.com says only gone, and Forest Lookouts says removed. No source describes what remains.

visit.trail_note: Labelled drive-up on the Idaho Fire Lookouts page (dated July 4, 2022); no source says whether the road is open today

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Idaho Fire Lookouts says destroyed in 1950, firelookout.com says gone 1950 with no cause, and Forest Lookouts says removed with no date. The record keeps gone and reports all three.
firelookout.com names the Coeur d'Alene and Kootenai National Forests; Forest Lookouts names the Kootenai National Forest. The record uses firelookout.com's wording.
firelookout.com gives Shoshone County, Idaho and Sanders County, Montana. The site sits on the state line; both counties are reported.

notes_for_editor: Almost certainly the same tower as us-mt-divide-peak-seventy-two: both describe the 1931 pole tower on 72 Peak at the Montana-Idaho line, gone by 1950. The two records should be reconciled or linked. Coordinates: the brief point (47.97274, -116.03039) is firelookout.com's; the Montana record gives 47.96641, -116.02442 from the FFLA list; not resolved. Idaho Fire Lookouts has Weber family photos (1937, 1939, 1971) of the site but the cached page gives no image URLs, so none are added. The Idaho writers say their first visit went to the wrong spot. No source describes remains or public access today.
